declarations.name: LkAccordion
declarations.description: <lk-accordion> turns child elements marked with data-lk-item="Title" into a set of collapsible sections (WAI-ARIA accordion pattern).

attributes.name: multiple
attributes.description: Allow several sections to be open at once. Without it, opening one section closes the others.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the section headings, 1 to 6 (default 3).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the group.

declarations.name: LkAlert
declarations.description: <lk-alert> is a message that sits in the page, such as a tip or a warning.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description: info (default), success, warning or danger.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description: Optional bold first line.

attributes.name: dismissible
attributes.description: Adds a close button. Fires lk-dismiss, then removes the alert.

attributes.name: live
attributes.description: Announce the alert when it appears. Use it only for alerts added after the page loads, such as a save error.

examples:
<lk-alert tone="warning" heading="Deadline moved" dismissible>
  Submit by Friday instead.
</lk-alert>

declarations.name: LkAvatar
declarations.description: <lk-avatar> shows a person as a picture, or as their initials when there is no picture or it fails to load.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The person's name. Used for the initials and the accessible name.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: Optional picture URL.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: sm, md (default) or lg.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description: A fixed colour (primary, success, warning, info, danger). By default the colour comes from the name, so it is stable.

attributes.name: decorative
attributes.description: Hide it from screen readers, for when the name is shown next to it.

examples:
<lk-avatar name="Ada Lovelace"></lk-avatar>
<lk-avatar name="Grace Hopper" src="grace.jpg" size="lg"></lk-avatar>

declarations.name: LkChip
declarations.description: <lk-chip> is a compact label. It can be plain, selectable (a toggle) or removable.

attributes.name: selectable
attributes.description: The label becomes a toggle button (aria-pressed).

attributes.name: selected
attributes.description: Current state of a selectable chip. Set it or read it.

attributes.name: removable
attributes.description: Adds a remove button. Fires lk-remove, then removes the chip.

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description: primary, success, warning, danger or info. Optional.

examples:
<lk-chip>Level 2</lk-chip>
<lk-chip selectable selected>Maths</lk-chip>
<lk-chip removable>Evening</lk-chip>

declarations.name: LkConversation
declarations.description: <lk-conversation> shows a conversation going back and forth, with the questions in it named. It is made for teaching good questioning, such as checking a claim from an AI chatbot. A learner can read it all at once or step through one message at a time, and can open a note on any message.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the whole conversation. Required.

attributes.name: stepped
attributes.description: Show one message at a time, with a "Show next message" button.

attributes.name: example
attributes.description: Say that the conversation is made up. Give it words to replace the default.

attributes.name: why-label
attributes.description: Words on the note button (default "Why this works").

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for thread titles, 1 to 6 (default 3).

examples:
Research shows learners retain 90% more.
Which study says that?

"Research shows" names no source. Ask where it comes from.

...messages...
...messages...

declarations.name: LkDrawer
declarations.description: <lk-drawer> is a panel that slides in from the side of the screen, for navigation, filters or details that should not take over the page. It is a modal dialog underneath: focus stays inside while it is open, the page behind is inert, and Escape or a click outside closes it.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: start or end (default end). It follows the reading direction.

examples:
<button data-lk-open="filters">Filters</button>
<lk-drawer id="filters" heading="Filter courses" side="start">...</lk-drawer>

declarations.name: LkField
declarations.description: <lk-field> adds a label, hint and error message to a native text-like control (input, select or textarea) and wires up the ARIA for you.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Visible label text. Required for accessibility.

attributes.name: hint
attributes.description: Help text shown under the label.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Error message. Set it from your own validation; clear it to remove.

declarations.name: LkChoices
declarations.description: <lk-choices> groups checkboxes or radio buttons into a fieldset with a legend, hint and error. Put plain `<label><input ...> Text</label>` children inside it.

attributes.name: legend
attributes.description: Visible group label. Required for accessibility.

attributes.name: hint
attributes.description: Help text shown under the legend.

attributes.name: error
attributes.description: Error message from your own validation.

attributes.name: min
attributes.description: Minimum number of checked boxes, for checkbox groups.

declarations.name: LkFlashcards
declarations.description: <lk-flashcards> is a stack of cards for recall practice. The learner reads the front, tries to remember the back, reveals it, then says whether they knew it. Cards they did not know come round again until all are known.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

attributes.name: shuffle
attributes.description: Present the cards in a random order.

examples:
Assessment during learning, used to shape the teaching.
Assessment at the end, used to judge what was learned.

declarations.name: LkFlow
declarations.description: <lk-flow> draws a process or a decision tree from nested lists, and can walk a learner through it one choice at a time.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

attributes.name: layout
attributes.description: process (default) or tree. A tree never rejoins: every branch ends in a result, and nothing can follow a decision.

attributes.name: walkthrough
attributes.description: Adds a panel that asks one question at a time, shows the route taken and highlights it on the chart.

examples:
1. Work arrives after the deadline
  2. Was an extension agreed?
    • Mark as normal
    • Apply the late penalty
  3. Return feedback

declarations.name: LkGlossary
declarations.description: <lk-glossary> shows a list of terms and their meanings, sorted A to Z, with a search box and jump links for each letter. Write the terms in any order.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Name for the glossary. Required.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the letter headings, 1 to 6 (default 3).

examples:
<lk-glossary label="Key terms">
  <dl>
    <dt>Formative assessment</dt>
    <dd>Checking progress during learning, to help it along.</dd>
    <dt>Summative assessment</dt>
    <dd>Judging what has been learned at the end.</dd>
  </dl>
</lk-glossary>

declarations.name: LkGridExplorer
declarations.description: <lk-grid-explorer> shows a grid of tiles. Choosing a tile reveals its details below, and the grid tracks which tiles have been explored.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the grid. Required.

attributes.name: columns
attributes.description: Number of columns, 1 to 6 (default 3). Narrow screens use fewer.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the detail title, 1 to 6 (default 3).

examples:
Learning as a change in behaviour...
Learners build knowledge...

declarations.name: LkHotspot
declarations.description: <lk-hotspot> puts numbered points on a picture or diagram. Choosing a point shows its explanation, and the component tracks which have been explored.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

examples:
Makes seeds.
Carries water.

declarations.name: LkJournal
declarations.description: <lk-journal> is a reflection journal: a set of prompts with a text box each. Notes are saved in this browser as the learner types, and can be copied or downloaded.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Storage key for this journal. Required if you want notes kept. Use a different name for each journal on your site.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Visible title, also used in exports.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the title, 1 to 6 (default 2).

attributes.name: rows
attributes.description: Height of each text box in rows (default 5).

declarations.name: LkMatrix
declarations.description: <lk-matrix> turns a native table into an activity. Cells the learner must complete are marked in the markup; every other cell stays as written. The table reads normally without JavaScript.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Instruction for the activity. Required.

attributes.name: show-answers
attributes.description: Adds a "Show answers" button after the learner has checked.

examples:
Learning theories
FocusActive learner
BehaviourismBehaviour
ConstructivismMeaning

declarations.name: LkMenu
declarations.description: <lk-menu> is a button that opens a list of actions or links.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Text on the trigger button. Required.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Optional lk-button variant for the trigger (primary, danger, link).

examples: Export

declarations.name: LkModal
declarations.description: <lk-modal> wraps its content in a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), so the browser provides the top layer, focus containment, an inert background and the Escape key. LearnKit adds the heading, close button, backdrop click, focus return and trigger wiring.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description: Visible title. Gives the dialog its accessible name.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name to use when there is no visible heading.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the title, 1 to 6 (default 2).

attributes.name: static
attributes.description: Do not close when the backdrop is clicked. Escape and the close button still work.

attributes.name: close-label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the close button (default "Close").

declarations.name: LkBreadcrumbs
declarations.description: <lk-breadcrumbs> shows where the learner is in a hierarchy.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name (default "Breadcrumb").

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: Longest trail to show. Middle items collapse behind a button that reveals them.

examples:
1. Home
  2. Courses
  3. Maths

declarations.name: LkPagination
declarations.description: <lk-pagination> moves between pages of results.

attributes.name: total
attributes.description: Number of pages.

attributes.name: page
attributes.description: Current page (1-based). Change it at any time.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name (default "Pagination").

attributes.name: siblings
attributes.description: Pages shown either side of the current one (default 1).

examples: <lk-pagination label="Results" total="12" page="1"></lk-pagination>

declarations.name: LkOrder
declarations.description: <lk-order> asks the learner to put items in the right sequence. Write the items in the CORRECT order; they are shuffled for the learner.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Question or instruction. Required.

attributes.name: pickup
attributes.description: Adds Pick up and Place buttons.

examples:
1. Plan
  2. Draft
  3. Revise
  4. Publish

declarations.name: LkTooltip
declarations.description: <lk-tooltip> shows a short hint when its target is hovered or focused.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: Id of the target element.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: top, bottom, left or right (default top). It flips when there is no room.

examples:
<button id="help">Help</button>
<lk-tooltip for="help">Opens the course guide</lk-tooltip>

declarations.name: LkPopover
declarations.description: <lk-popover> is a small panel of content that opens next to a trigger. Unlike a tooltip it can hold links, buttons and form controls.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: top, bottom, left or right (default bottom).

examples:
<button data-lk-popover="info">More about this</button>
<lk-popover id="info" label="About this topic">...</lk-popover>

declarations.name: LkProcess
declarations.description: <lk-process> walks a learner through steps, one at a time, with a stepper showing where they are. Each step is a child marked with data-lk-step.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for step titles, 1 to 6 (default 3).

examples:
Decide what learners will be able to do...
...

declarations.name: LkProgress
declarations.description: <lk-progress> shows how far along something is.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Current value. Leave it out for an indeterminate bar.

attributes.name: max
attributes.description: Maximum value (default 100).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name, for example "Course progress". Required.

attributes.name: show-value
attributes.description: Also show the percentage as text.

declarations.name: LkStepper
declarations.description: <lk-stepper> marks where the learner is in an ordered list of steps. It shows progress; it does not hold the content of the steps.

attributes.name: current
attributes.description: Zero-based index of the current step (default 0). Change it at any time. Steps before it are complete.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the list.

attributes.name: compact
attributes.description: Show only the current step’s label. Added for you when there are more than five steps. The other labels stay available to screen readers.

examples:
1. Your details
  2. Choose a course
  3. Confirm

declarations.name: LkQuiz
declarations.description: <lk-quiz> is a knowledge check: one question at a time, instant feedback, then a score. Write the questions as markup, as JSON, or both.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the quiz.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Visible title (the JSON title is used if this is missing).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for the title and results, 1 to 6 (default 2).

attributes.name: shuffle
attributes.description: Shuffle the order of the options each attempt.

examples:
A quick quiz
A final exam

Formative assessment happens during learning.

declarations.name: LkRating
declarations.description: <lk-rating> is a self-assessment: the learner rates themselves on a scale for one or more statements.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Group name. Required.

attributes.name: scale
attributes.description: Number of points, 2 to 10 (default 5).

attributes.name: low
attributes.description: Description of the lowest point.

attributes.name: high
attributes.description: Description of the highest point.

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: Show an average and areas to focus on once every statement is rated.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Storage key. If set, ratings are remembered in this browser.

declarations.name: LkRespond
declarations.description: <lk-respond> shows a set of situations, such as posts in a feed. For each one the learner picks a response, reads what would happen, then checks them all together. More than one response can be suitable for a situation.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the whole activity. Required.

attributes.name: question
attributes.description: The question under each situation (default "What would you do?").

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for each case title, 1 to 6 (default 3).

attributes.name: explanation-label
attributes.description: Optional words shown before each explanation, such as "Why".

examples:
"The council has cancelled every election. Share this before it is deleted!"

Sharing spreads an unchecked claim.
Ask for evidence, calmly.
You avoid amplifying it, but others may believe it.

Check credible sources before sharing.

declarations.name: LkScenario
declarations.description: <lk-scenario> is a branching story. The learner reads a situation, chooses what to do, and sees where it leads.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

attributes.name: start
attributes.description: Id of the first node (default: the first node).

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for node titles, 1 to 6 (default 3).

examples:
A learner asks for more time...

  • Say no
  • Agree an extension
...
...

declarations.name: LkSort
declarations.description: <lk-sort> asks the learner to sort items into groups. Write each item under the group where it BELONGS; the items are shuffled into a pile for the learner.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Instruction for the activity. Required.

attributes.name: pickup
attributes.description: Adds Pick up and Place buttons.

examples:
• A quiz in class
  • Feedback on a draft
  • A final exam

declarations.name: LkSpectrum
declarations.description: <lk-spectrum> asks a learner to place their view between two poles, then compares it with an expert position.

attributes.name: statement
attributes.description: The question or statement. Required.

attributes.name: expert
attributes.description: Expert position, 0 (left) to 100 (right). Without it there is no comparison step.

attributes.name: explanation
attributes.description: Why the expert holds that position. Shown on comparing.

examples:
<lk-spectrum statement="How should feedback be given?"
             left="Written" right="Spoken" expert="70"
             explanation="Spoken feedback allows a conversation, but write down the key points.">
</lk-spectrum>

declarations.name: LkSwitch
declarations.description: <lk-switch> is an on/off setting, built on a native checkbox with role="switch" so it works in forms and with every assistive technology.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Required.

examples: <lk-switch label="Email reminders" hint="One a week" name="reminders" checked></lk-switch>

declarations.name: LkTable
declarations.description: <lk-table> makes a native <table> sortable and filterable. The table stays ordinary HTML, so it reads well without JavaScript.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the scrolling region. Required.

attributes.name: sortable
attributes.description: Header cells become sort buttons. Put data-nosort on a <th> to skip it.

attributes.name: filter
attributes.description: Adds a search box that hides rows without every typed word.

attributes.name: striped
attributes.description: Shades alternate rows.

examples:
...
Courses this term
CourseHours

declarations.name: LkTabs
declarations.description: <lk-tabs> turns child elements marked with data-lk-tab="Title" into an accessible tabbed interface (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, manual activation off).

attributes.name: selected
attributes.description: Zero-based index of the initially selected tab (default 0).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the tab list.

declarations.name: LkTimeline
declarations.description: <lk-timeline> lays out events in order. Each event is a child marked with data-lk-date.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name for the list.

attributes.name: level
attributes.description: Heading level for event titles, 1 to 6 (default 3).

attributes.name: collapsible
attributes.description: Event details open and close when the title is pressed.

attributes.name: stepped
attributes.description: Show one event at a time. A button reveals the next.

examples:
The first classes began...
...

declarations.name: LkToasts
declarations.description: <lk-toasts> is the region that holds notifications. You rarely write it by hand: call toast() and one is created for you. Add one yourself to choose where notifications appear.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: top-start, top-end, bottom-start or bottom-end (default).

examples: <lk-toasts placement="top-end"></lk-toasts>

declarations.name: LkTree
declarations.description: <lk-tree> shows nested content that can be opened and closed, such as a course outline. Write it as nested lists.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Accessible name. Required.

examples:
• Unit 1
    • Lesson A
    • Lesson B
  • Unit 2
    • Lesson C
